messages.subject: need Jacobian warning
parts:
[changed subject/thread]

Thanks for the reminder.

I'm going to try to make that warning a little more
nuanced in detection and add some tests. I'm adding
the fix to feature/c++11, so that should hold off until
this is pushed for more testing.

- Bob


On Mar 5, 2014, at 7:25 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:

> On Wednesday, March 5, 2014 12:12:27 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> Won't work if we pass by const reference. Also, direct
> access of lp__ is deprecated. We decided we'd rather not
> give users that much rope with which to hang themselves. (They
> [and we] were making mistakes like setting rather than incrementing,
> thereby bypassing the Jacobians on the constraints.)
>
> On that point, the parser warning is still phrased in terms of the old way
>
> DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
>
> Warning (non-fatal): sampling statement (~) contains a transformed parameter or local variable.
> You must increment lp__ with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
> Sampling Statement left-hand-side expression:
> sigma2 ~ inv_gamma_log(...)
>
>
> So, it should say something to the effect of: You need to do increment_log_prob(LOG_ABS_JACOBIAN_DETERMINANT);
>
> Ben
>
> On Mar 5, 2014, at 5:09 PM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
>
> > What if you had to explicitly list it as an argument?
> >
> >
> > On Wed, Mar 5, 2014 at 10:40 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> > It could, but I really think that was a very poor choice on
> > my part to begin with given the popularity of log! So I'd
> > rather choose something else if we do it explicitly, like maybe
> > _lp?
> >
> > - Bob
> >
> > On Mar 4, 2014, at 4:09 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > > Can the user-defined function end with _log and get lp__ passed to it automatically?
> > >
> > > Ben
> > >
> > > On Tuesday, March 4, 2014 8:28:51 AM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> > > One thing I just realized is that if we prohibit access to increment_log_prob
> > > in functions and restrict it to submodels, there'll be no way to write
> > > natural transform functions, as in:
> > >
> > > real logit_inverse_transform(real logit_a) {
> > > real a;
> > > a <- inv_logit(logit_a);
> > > increment_log_prob(log(a) + log1m(a));
> > > return a;
> > > }
> > >
> > > Instead, we'd need to write the function and then a Jacobian
> > > submodel and make sure to call both.
> > >
> > > I could add lp__ as an implicit argument to functions, and
> > > set it to a dummy double value for blocks other than transformed
> > > parameters and model. Would that be too confusing?
> > >
> > > - Bob
> > >
